newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Guangxi to set up national sugar market.
newsitem.headline: China's Guangxi to set up national sugar market.

text.p: China's southwestern Guangxi region, the country's top sugar producer, plans to set up a national wholesale market to boost trade, the China Business Daily said on Wednesday.
The region plans to boost the scale of existing sugar wholesale markets to become a national market, the newspaper said.
The sugar market would be jointly managed by the Ministry of Internal Trade, the China Council of Light Industry and the Guangxi regional government, it said.
Currently, the Guangxi Sugar Co operates separate sugar wholesale markets in the capital Nanning and Liuzhou, it said.
Trading was slight because most sugar traders preferred deals outside the markets, it said, but gave no further details.
The Guangxi government would draft regulations and take measures to force sugar firms to focus their trading on the markets, the newspaper said.
Banks would boost loans to sugar factories that sell more on the markets while reducing lending to firms that sell less, it said.
